text: The business requirements of the business epic and the PRD of rwb-comms are treated as readable but not approved, and the two stories of this key are written with Status Draft (realignment v1); no approval blocks the split.
why: No approved status or approval record is available in this run and the realignment requires no human approval to proceed (D-RCV-60 overlay, AGENTS.md rule 9).
read: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-037); FSD P6 Communications v3 (status In review); TSD P6 Communications v2 (status In review)
impact: Low: status and approval only; no scope, value or date is affected.

text: The self-service payment surface of RWB-E4-037 is new on the comms base: the two operations and the PaymentInstruction resource are declared under /api/recovery/comms/v1, and the rwb-payment registration and the rwb-source-data contact read are declared as consumed and faked with an empty Contract dependencies row, because the plan names no contract story of either service for this key.
why: The legacy story has no operation of its own, the TSD P6 inventory holds no self-service operation and the P6 ownership rows hold no payment resource, while the act needs the money of P8 and the contact facts of P1.
read: RWB-E4-037 Endpoints and Data tables; FSD P6 A2.16; TSD P6 T-A.1 and T6.1; context pack P6 (ownership rows, slides 4, 10 and 13)
confirm: Solution architect; owners of P8 rwb-payment and P1 rwb-source-data
impact: Medium: the app story builds against fakes of two owners until their contracts exist, and the C rows are added when those contract stories are planned.

text: The reference of the latest registered self-service payment is held as a nullable column on the notice of rwb_comms; its name is fixed by RWB-P6-E4037-CON and its value is the payment reference the owner answers.
why: The legacy data table ties the act to the notice and gives no column for it, the Logical Data Model gives it no field ID, and the notice is the only P6 row the act can be recorded against.
read: RWB-E4-037 Data table (notice, DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-023); TSD P6 T3.1; Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 (notice fields)
impact: Low: one nullable column with no default and no backfill; the value stays the owner's reference.

text: The capability area and the right of the two self-service operations are declared as Case record with the customer scope applied, taken from the Case record column of the role and right matrix of TSD P6 T6.1, and each operation authorises the object as well as the action so that only the customer's own case answers.
why: No source states the right of a self-service act and the FSD gives the customer (borrower) as the only primary role of FEAT-COM-03.
read: TSD P6 T6.1 and T6.2; FSD P6 A2.16.3.3; context pack P6 (slide 10: each service authorises the object itself)
impact: Medium: a wrong right would widen or close the self-service surface; the scope check on the case limits the exposure.

text: The consent state per channel and the contact stop that the conduct check of A2.16 needs are read from the rwb-source-data contract over v_ace_contact, one hop with a 2 s budget, and are faked until that contract exists; this service holds no contact table, no contact-point extension row and no v_ace_* grant.
why: The contact repository tables are not among the P6 ownership rows, the module reads contact points from v_ace_contact plus contact_point_ext, and DP-05 sends ACE data through the source-data contract or the service's own views, of which this service has none.
read: FSD P6 A2.16.3.1 (VR-P6-016-1, VR-P6-016-2) and A2.18; TSD P6 T3.1; context pack P6 (ownership rows, DP-05, slide 8)
confirm: Owner of P1 rwb-source-data; compliance and PDPA officer
impact: Medium: the check fails closed until the owner answers, so no payment is registered on an unverified contact fact.

text: The payment event that rwb-comms consumes from rwb-payment is declared on rwb.payment.events.v1 with its name left as a placeholder, because the read material names no event of rwb-payment although the connection matrix draws the listen arrow from P6 to P8.
why: Architecture v5 slide 13 marks E (listens to events) in the P8 column of the P6 row, and no source gives the event names of P8; naming one would invent a value.
read: Context pack P6 (slide 13 connection matrix, row P6 Comms); Architecture v5 slide 42 event catalogue as summarised in the pack
confirm: Owner of P8 rwb-payment; event platform owner
impact: Low: the consumed row is declared and faked; the name is filled when the P8 event catalogue is published.
